u^*(t)
=   \eexp^{-itH} u_0 - i \int_0^t \diff s \eexp^{-i(t-s)H} (f(s) - B(s) u^*(s)).

issues.failure_explanation: For the equation (i∂t−H−B)u=f, Duhamel's formula is u(t)=e^{-itH}u0−i∫e^{-i(t-s)H}(f(s)+B(s)u(s))ds. The displayed formula with f−Bu solves instead (i∂t−H+B)u=f. The fixed-point proof in the appendix repeats the same sign, so it establishes existence for the wrong sign.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace f(s)−B(s)u(s) by f(s)+B(s)u(s) in the Duhamel formula and in the fixed-point map.
issues.overall_effect: The stated Duhamel representation in Proposition XX properties is false, and the existence/uniqueness proof for B≠0 in the appendix does not prove the stated equation.
issues.title: Sign error in Duhamel formula for time-dependent B
issues.why_classification: A single forced sign correction preserves all substantive claims and the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes equivalence with the XX_H0 norm, which under v=e^{itH0}u is (|v(0)|^2+T||∂t v||^2)^{1/2}. This is not equivalent to the standard H^1 norm with constants independent of T. For v-v*=constant c, sqrt(F(v)) is at least |c| while ||v-v*||_{H^1}=√T|c|, so the upper bound fails for small T.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the H^1 norm by the transported XX_H0 norm (|v(0)|^2+T||∂t v||^2)^{1/2} or state estimates with explicit T-dependent equivalence factors.
issues.overall_effect: The H^1 error estimate and the advertised T-independent constants in Corollary variational formulation v and Theorem th:Schro are false. Downstream Galerkin error estimates in H^1 inherit the issue.
issues.title: T-independent H^1 estimate uses wrong norm
issues.why_classification: The variational formulation remains valid, but the stated norm and T-independent constants require a nontrivial correction that changes the error estimates.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: F(v) = \abs{v(0) - u_0}^2 + T \norm{(i\partial_t - \eexp^{itH_0} (A + B(t)) \eexp^{-itH_0}) v - \eexp^{itH_0} f}_{\Ltwosp{I, \HHilb}}^2

issues.failure_explanation: The functional and the equation include B(t), but the proof computes the residual with A only. For B≠0, F(v) is not equal to ||u-u*||_XX_H^2; the missing B term invalidates the inference.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Carry A+B(t) instead of A throughout the computation and use the time-dependent norm equivalence.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Corollary variational formulation v does not establish the result when B≠0.
issues.title: Proof of Corollary variational formulation omits B
issues.why_classification: A local replacement of A by A+B repairs the proof without changing the statement.

issues.failure_explanation: Membership in Y_{H0} requires (i∂t−H0)u∈L2. For unbounded H0, a general w∈C_c^∞(I,H) does not satisfy this, so C_c^∞(I,H) is not a subset of Y_{H0}. The proof must use test functions in C_c^∞(I,D(H0)) (or similar).

failure_location.tag: prop: S-star connection with the PDE

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Take w in C_c^∞(I,D(H0)) so that w∈Y_{H0} and the integration-by-parts computation is justified.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the dual characterization of the PDE is incomplete; the subsequent L2 dual formulation lacks a valid proof.
issues.primary_affected_tag: prop: S-star connection with the PDE
issues.title: Invalid test-function space in dual formulation proof
issues.why_classification: A standard domain correction for the test functions fixes the proof locally.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: (A2) The operator $A$ is a closed symmetric operator on $\HHilb$ such that $D(H_0) \subset D(A)$.
is a strongly convex quadratic functional defined on $\Ltwosp{I, \HHilb}$

issues.failure_explanation: The expression contains A u inside an integral. By (A2), A is only defined on D(A), not on all of L2. For arbitrary u∈L2(I,H), A u is not defined, so E^* is not a functional on L2 as claimed. This includes the main Coulomb-potential application.

failure_location.quote: \norm{u(t) + i \int_0^t \diff s \eexp^{-i(t-s)H_0}(Au) - \left( \eexp^{-itH_0} u_0 - i \int_0^t \diff s \eexp^{-i(t-s)H_0} f(s) \right)}_{\Ltwosp{I, \HHilb}}^2

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the domain to a subspace where A u is defined (e.g., u∈XX_H or a suitable D(A)-valued Bochner space), which changes the advertised L2 formulation.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised dual formulation on L2 is not well-defined for unbounded A; the corollary's domain and convexity claim fail.
issues.title: Dual L2 functional is undefined for unbounded A
issues.why_classification: The result as stated is ill-defined for the intended unbounded operators, and a supported repair necessarily changes the domain and loses the L2 formulation.
